subject: Questions on DPA Annex, Cross-Border Delegation & DPF Evidence for NovusCare RFP
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novuscare.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com, NovusCare RFP <rfp@novuscare.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel.park@novuscare.com>
Date: Tue, 23 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA questions: delegation, DPF evidence, and subprocessors

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for your help so far on the RFP. Procurement and our privacy team have a few follow-up clarifications for the DPA annex and international transfer evidence so we can clear legal review: 

1) Controller / Processor classification: please confirm whether Redwood is signing the DPA as a processor and confirm any scenarios where you would be controller.

2) Transfer mechanisms: we need an explicit statement of which legal transfer mechanisms Redwood relies on for EU -> US processing (SCCs, EU-US DPF, UK Addendum, etc.) and the order of precedence when multiple mechanisms are applicable.

3) Onward transfers & subprocessors: provide your current subprocessor list, the geographic regions where those subprocessors may process EU personal data, and confirmation whether you allow customers to require location restrictions as part of the DPA annex.

4) Evidence: NovusCare needs a copy of any current DPF self-certification evidence, SOC2 Type II report (redacted if needed), penetration test summary, and your DPA annex template.

I've attached a short PDF with the specific Annex Qs (NovusCare_RFP_Annex_Questions.pdf). Our committee is meeting Wednesday the 24th — can you let us know if this is feasible on an expedited timeline?

Best,
Elena

From: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com, lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 23 May 2028 11:03:48 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA questions: delegation, DPF evidence, and subprocessors

Attaching a first-pass evidence bundle: Redwood_DPF_Supplemental_Evidence.zip (contains DPF self-certification snapshot, SOC2 Type II redacted, pen-test exec summary, and our DPA Annex template).

High-level answers we can provide now (for Elena's committee):
- Processor role: Redwood operates as a processor when we process customer prompt/input data for model inference. We do not determine purposes of processing for customer data; customers remain controller. We may be controller only for limited product telemetry used for platform health where data is aggregated and not attributed.
- Transfer mechanisms: our baseline approach is to implement the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) between customer and Redwood for transfers from the EEA/UK to the US. Where both parties agree, Redwood's EU-US Data Privacy Framework (DPF) self-certification can be referenced as an additional transparency / oversight measure; SCCs remain the contractual transfer mechanism in the DPA Annex.
- Subprocessors (current, high level):
  • Cloud compute / model serving: AWS (us-west-2), GCP (europe-west1) for multi-cloud dedicated pools
  • Storage / object store: AWS S3 (us-west-2), GCP Storage (europe-west1)
  • CDN / edge: Cloudflare (global)
  • Monitoring & logging: Datadog (logging redaction applied), Sentry (error telemetry)
  • Identity & key management integrations: AWS KMS, GCP KMS; customer-managed keys supported for Dedicated/Private
\- On location restrictions: we can accept reasonable, scoped location restrictions in the DPA Annex (for example, restrict processing to EU only for the model input/outputs) provided the restriction is compatible with the chosen deployment (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private). For Hosted customers that require strict EU-only processing, we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment.

Action items we will send: evidence zip, current subprocessor spreadsheet, and a redline of our standard DPA Annex that adds a clause for customer-requested location restrictions and the precedence statement about SCCs + DPF.

Attachment: Redwood_DPF_Supplemental_Evidence.zip (contains: DPF_cert_snapshot.pdf, SOC2_TypeII_redacted.pdf, pentest_summary.pdf, DPA_Annex_Template.docx)

-Marissa

From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novuscare.com>

Subject: Re: DPA questions: delegation, DPF evidence, and subprocessors

Karthik / Marissa — thank you for the quick turnaround and the evidence bundle. A couple of clarifying points from legal: 

• Precedence: we need an explicit contract clause that when SCCs are applied they govern transfers. If you also reference DPF in the evidence pack, we need to see that DPF is not being used to circumvent SCC obligations. Can you provide suggested wording that places SCCs as the primary contractual mechanism and DPF as an ancillary compliance posture?

• Subprocessor location restriction: NovusCare may need to restrict processing to EU-only for model inference of certain PHI fields. Will Redwood accept a carve-out for those data elements to be processed only in EU-based Dedicated or Private deployments, and will you accept a DPA redline that requires prior written approval for any subprocessor additions?

• Timeline: we need signed DPA + evidence by EOD 2028-05-25 to proceed to procurement approval on 05/26. Is that achievable?

I've attached our draft annex for redline (NovusCare_Annex_Draft.docx). Please confirm next steps and whether legal needs to be looped in on your side for an accelerated review.

Regards,
Elena

---
Attachment: NovusCare_Annex_Draft.docx

From: karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@novuscare.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 24 May 2028 16:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA questions: delegation, DPF evidence, and subprocessors - proposed next steps

Elena — thanks, and appreciate the clear asks.

Short answers and next steps: 
1) Precedence wording: we will propose this clause in the DPA Annex: "The Parties agree that the EU Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) shall constitute the primary contractual transfer mechanism for transfers of personal data from the EEA/UK to jurisdictions outside the EEA/UK. Where Redwood has voluntarily self-certified under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework (DPF), such self-certification shall operate as an additional transparency and oversight measure and shall not substitute or reduce the contractual protections afforded by the SCCs." We'll deliver a redline showing this placement.

2) EU-only processing carve-out: Redwood will accept scoped, data-element specific restrictions requiring EU-only processing provided the customer uses Dedicated or Private deployment that guarantees EU residency. For Hosted customers we can discuss geo-routing + Dedicated burst pools but cannot guarantee pure EU-only processing without Dedicated/Private. We will accept a DPA redline requiring prior written approval for subprocessor additions and will commit to 30 days' notice for most subprocessor changes (exceptions for security fixes will be handled per the DPA).

3) Timeline: yes — we can provide a DPA Annex redline and final evidence pack by EOD 2028-05-25. Lauren will be your point of contact for subprocessor confirmation; Marissa will upload the final evidence ZIP to the shared Drive link and we will deliver the DPA redline as Redwood_DPA_Annex_Redline.docx. Please confirm the email to send the signed DPA to (DocuSign link?) and whether you want legal-to-legal redline exchange or a single consolidated redline from Redwood first.

We will attach the redline and the final evidence set in our next message.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this quickly.

Best,
